pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/alerts/routing.rs:155 Webhook signing is opt-in per channel (`#[serde(default)] signed: bool`, so it defaults to false), and the env bench webhook and ntfy channels are never signed, so by default a receiver cannot tell a platform breach alert from a forged POST; the standard requires every delivered payload to carry a signature.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/alerts/routing.rs:155 Vetting is strong: https only, private/link-local/NAT64 refusal at configure and delivery time, Policy::none() redirects, 5s timeout, 2 KiB control-stripped response cap. But signing is opt-in and off by default, there is no channel-secret rotation route (prev_secret_hash is always None at create), and there is no destination allowlist setting.

crates/api/src/alerts/ledger.rs:50 Attribution, durable admission and per-channel HTTP all run in a spawned task. Each sink failure is logged and recorded as a Delivery row, never sent back to ingest.

crates/api/src/alerts/mod.rs:234 Breach key is project:metric:window:scope and the warn tier has its own key space. Ledger outage degrades to delivering anyway (ledger.rs:241-245), and rejection-flush keys carry the flush instant (compose.rs:514-517).

crates/api/src/alerts/attribution.rs:230 Top 3 sorted by cost, zero-spend rows dropped, share computed against the window total, with share and $ shown. Built from existing cost/use-case rollups inside the spawned task, pure compose split from fetch, store errors degrade to empty, and text and JSON come from one Attribution.

crates/api/src/alerts/attribution.rs:122 A model cap breaks down by use-case, a use-case cap by model, a provider cap by its models. Scoped rows are filtered first and shares use the within-scope total. An empty scope states 'no attributable spend in window'.

crates/api/src/alerts/attribution.rs:150 Key/customer scopes get no contributors, just a scope note pointing at GET /v1/limits/usage. Customer-axis forecast alerts are also stripped in compose::forecast_body.

crates/api/src/alerts/ledger.rs:89 Forecast alerts go through the same cooldown and durable gate using the methodology-free ForecastAlert key, and channel severity is tiered from the forecast. Only delivery is judged here; the forecast-driven enforcement is judged on its own contexts.

pairs.subject: breach-alerting-and-attribution
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/limits/rule.rs:234 While a forecast-stamped escalation is live, `effective_action_at` replaces the rule's configured action with `Escalation::to`, so a projection changes how traffic is enforced (e.g. starting to shed under Throttle before any measured breach); the technique says forecasts stay advisory and must not trigger enforcement.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/limits/rule.rs:234 Escalation is opt-in per rule, reversible and self-expiring (max 720h), but it is still forecast-triggered enforcement.
crates/core/src/limits/status.rs:195 alert_key = project:metric:window:scope_tag. It does not include value, ratio or how the breach was detected.

crates/core/src/alert_sign.rs:88 The shared primitive signs the exact body bytes with a server-time t, rejects stale timestamps on verify, emits one v1 per key during rotation, and compares in constant time. The opt-in signing policy lives in the api routing and is judged there. Note: alert_channel.rs:18 calls webhooks 'signed', which is only true when a key exists.

pairs.registryProposal: pre-breach-forecasting says 'do not let forecast alerts trigger enforcement' without separating that from an operator-authored, opt-in, time-boxed, self-reverting escalation that shadows (never overwrites) the configured action. If the corpus means to allow that bounded case, the technique should say so and set its guardrails; if not, it should name this pattern as the failure explicitly.

pairs.evidence: crates/responder/src/webhook.rs:88 Signature and freshness checks run only when LIGHTTRACK_RESPONDER_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set; without it the receiver acts on any POST (spending a Claude run, possibly editing a repo), and on a non-loopback bind it only prints a startup warning.

techniques.evidence: crates/responder/src/webhook.rs:88 When a secret is configured, verification is correct: raw body bytes, the shared core verify, 300s tolerance, 401 on failure. The skip-when-unconfigured default is the 'URL secrecy instead of signing' posture the technique refuses.
crates/responder/src/webhook.rs:133 The responder ignores breach and forecast payloads, so the attribution, dedup and forecasting techniques have nothing to apply to here.

pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/margin_guardrails.rs:100 The forecast sweep's escalation pass stamps `escalated_until` on a limit rule whenever a budget_breach forecast's ETA reaches the rule's `on_eta_days`, turning a projection into an enforcement change, which pre-breach-forecasting forbids.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/margin_guardrails.rs:100 The forecast alerts themselves conform: advisory 'on track to … in about N days' wording (forecast_alerts.rs:94), an evidence floor plus burn-rate corroboration gate, and one shared build_alerts used by both sweep and handler. The forecast-to-enforcement escalation is the deviation.
crates/api/src/forecast_alerts.rs:49 Key is project, kind, subject (rule or customer) and tier. It has nothing about sweep vs on-demand, so the two paths share one cooldown.

crates/api/src/forecast.rs:306 Customer-axis margin alerts are marked identity-scoped where the axis is known. The pointed-at authenticated surface exists and is principal-scoped (limits_usage.rs:99).
crates/api/src/forecast.rs:135 The forecast handler hands alerts to notify_forecast, which spawns delivery, and returns the response without waiting on any sink.
